string: Every person needs a certain amount of consistent sleep to perform optimally. Research has shown your need is determined by your biology and lifestyle. Your sleep need remains the same throughout adulthood.

We estimate your sleep need by comparing how much sleep you usually get versus when you sleep longer than usual—something we call sleep rebound. This is because your body tries to make up the sleep it needs when you sleep longer than usual. When you sleep longer on the weekends your body is trying to lower your sleep debt.

Each morning, LUMI checks Apple Health for the previous night\'s sleep. If your sleep tracking app has sent data to Apple Health, RISE will use it instead of phone-motion based sleep detection.

Steps, movement and phone motion data are translated into daily predictions for when and how long you have slept. Use your phone as you normally would and LUMI will automatically track your sleep daily.
After completing these steps, you\'ll start receiving notifications from LUMI on your device

Notifications are crucial to RISE. They keep on track and help you optimize your routines by reminding you at the right time based on your daily energy schedule. Don\'t miss out on personalized energy-based nudges for work, rest, sleep, and more.

To customize notifications in RISE, go to \"Settings\" on your iPhone, select RISE, and choose the notification style. To adjust a specific reminder, swipe up on the shortcuts tray above the tabs, and tap the reminder to customize.

LUMI publishes your Peak Energy and Dip Energy calendars to your calendar daily. When you open your calendar you\'ll see your energy times blocked out for the next 7 days to help you plan according to your energy.
Your timekeeping preference will determine the clock used for time references in RISE. Your energy schedule, reminders, sleep times, etc will all switch to display the clock of your choice.
The 12-hour clock is a time convention in which the 24 hours of the day are divided into two periods: a.m. and p.m.

The 24-hour clock, popularly referred to as military time, is the convention of timekeeping in which the day runs from midnight to midnight and is divided into 24 hours. This is indicated by the hours passed since midnight, from 0 to 23.

Your iPhone’s language preference will determine the language used by RISE on first use, if the app supports it. You can always switch languages. If you feel the translations are not as good as our primary language, English, please let us know as we are working on improving those and adding more language support.
